item.title: [PBV7-488] Expose and operate the gateway through Traefik and MetalLB
item.description:
Source and parent

Specification: Realtime WebSocket Platform – .NET 10, Redis, and Kubernetes
Parent Epic: PBV7-484

Context

Securely expose the independently deployed gateway through Traefik and MetalLB while preserving service during rolling updates, pod failures, and node maintenance.

Requirements

  • Publish the gateway only through its ClusterIP Service.
  • Configure Traefik WSS routing for realtime.propago.local and the approved WebSocket path.
  • Terminate TLS at Traefik unless an approved environment requires end-to-end TLS.
  • Integrate the approved certificate source and renewal process.
  • Preserve required Host, Forwarded, and Origin behavior and redact sensitive access-log values.
  • Ensure response buffering and ordinary request retry behavior are not applied to upgraded connections.
  • Configure Traefik and upstream timeouts longer than the application heartbeat interval.
  • Run sufficient Traefik replicas and apply topology/disruption controls.
  • Define and validate the MetalLB IPAddressPool and Layer 2 or BGP advertisement strategy.
  • Document the Layer 2/BGP selection and externalTrafficPolicy decision.
  • Preserve source IP when required and prove the observed behavior.
  • Implement gateway readiness withdrawal, connection drain, client service-restart notification, bounded shutdown, and Kubernetes termination timing.
  • Add edge and infrastructure metrics for Traefik, certificates, MetalLB controller/speakers, VIP advertisement, deployment health, and rollout state where supported.
  • Extend deployment validation automation to verify DNS, certificate chain, WSS upgrade, long-lived connection, routing, and failover.

Dependencies

  • Gateway and Redis functionality.
  • Kubernetes and Helm packaging.
  • Approved DNS, certificate, Traefik, MetalLB address range, and network-routing inputs.

Completion criteria

  • External clients connect through trusted WSS at realtime.propago.local.
  • Gateway pods are not directly exposed through MetalLB or NodePort.
  • A client can reconnect through another gateway pod after rollout or failure.
  • Traefik and MetalLB configuration is version controlled, reviewable, and environment scoped.
  • The selected traffic policy and source-IP behavior are documented and verified.
  • Rollback procedures cover route, certificate, application, and VIP configuration.

Testing criteria

  • Test WSS upgrade, correct host/path routing, allowed and rejected Origin values, certificate validation, and long-lived connections.
  • Test invalid route, invalid certificate, certificate renewal, timeout, and backend-unavailable behavior.
  • Restart Traefik pods and verify service recovery.
  • Delete and roll gateway pods and verify readiness withdrawal, bounded drain, client reconnect, and no routing to terminating pods.
  • Drain a worker node and verify replica redistribution and client recovery.
  • Test MetalLB speaker/controller disruption and VIP failover.
  • Verify Layer 2 or BGP advertisement from the intended nodes and network segments.
  • Verify source-IP behavior for the selected external traffic policy.
  • Confirm edge logs and metrics identify handshake, routing, TLS, timeout, and backend errors without exposing credentials.
